subject: microbiology
title: FTA ABS, Dark-Ground Microscopy, Chancre and Congenital Syphilis

steps.tx: **FTA ABS** is the fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption test. Serum is first absorbed with nonpathogenic treponemal material to remove cross-reactive antibodies, then applied to Treponema pallidum fixed on a slide and detected with fluorescent antihuman antibody. It becomes positive early and usually remains positive for life. The labour-intensive manual method has largely been replaced by automated treponemal immunoassays, TPPA and line immunoassays.
steps.say: FTA ABS confirmed treponemal infection historically, but absorbed serum and fluorescence interpretation limit routine use.

left.title: Method
points: Absorption removes group treponemal cross reactivity
Patient antibody binds fixed Nichols strain organisms
Fluorescent conjugate reveals antibody binding
Reactive intensity is graded under ultraviolet microscopy

right.title: Interpretation
points: Positive early in primary syphilis
Usually lifelong despite treatment
Cannot judge activity without RPR or VDRL trend
False positives occur with autoimmune and other treponemal disease

steps.tx: **Dark ground microscopy** makes living treponemes visible as bright, slender corkscrew organisms against a black background because oblique light is scattered by the specimen into the objective. It requires immediate examination of fresh serous exudate from a moist lesion, minimal blood contamination and an experienced observer. Characteristic slow rotation and bending support primary syphilis before seroconversion.
steps.say: Dark-field diagnosis depends on fresh lesion fluid and recognising slow corkscrew motility.

left.title: Good specimen
points: Clean lesion gently and collect serous exudate
Avoid antiseptics and topical antibiotics first
Examine immediately while organisms are motile
Genital lesions are more reliable than oral lesions

right.title: Pitfalls
points: Oral commensal treponemes can look similar
Blood and debris obscure organisms
Drying rapidly abolishes motility
One negative examination does not exclude syphilis

steps.tx: A syphilitic **chancre** begins as a papule that ulcerates into a characteristically painless, indurated lesion with a clean base and firm regional lymphadenopathy. Atypical painful or multiple lesions occur, especially with HSV coinfection or HIV. The chancre resolves spontaneously in several weeks, creating a dangerous false impression of cure while treponemes disseminate and secondary disease approaches.
steps.say: Spontaneous healing of a chancre means stage transition is possible, not that infection has ended.

left.title: Classic chancre
points: Single painless ulcer
Button like induration at base
Painless rubbery regional nodes
Serous rather than purulent exudate

right.title: Important mimics
points: Herpes simplex grouped painful vesicles and ulcers
Chancroid painful soft ulcer with tender bubo
Traumatic ulcer lacks induration
LGV ulcer is often transient and unnoticed

steps.tx: **Congenital syphilis** follows transplacental Treponema pallidum dissemination. Early disease can cause rhinitis or snuffles, widespread rash involving palms and soles, hepatosplenomegaly, anaemia, osteochondritis and periostitis. Late stigmata include Hutchinson incisors, mulberry molars, interstitial keratitis, sensorineural deafness, saddle nose and frontal bossing. Maternal screening and adequate treatment at least thirty days before delivery prevent most cases.
steps.say: Congenital syphilis is preventable when maternal infection is screened and treated early enough.

left.title: Early congenital
points: Snuffles and maculopapular rash
Pemphigus syphiliticus on palms and soles
Hepatosplenomegaly and jaundice
Painful limbs from osteochondritis

right.title: Late stigmata
points: Notched Hutchinson incisors
Interstitial keratitis
Eighth cranial nerve deafness
Saddle nose and Clutton joints

steps.tx: Infant evaluation compares infant and maternal **quantitative nontreponemal titres**, physical findings, long bone imaging, cerebrospinal fluid studies and placental or umbilical molecular or pathological testing where available. Transplacental maternal IgG makes a reactive treponemal test expected in exposed infants, so a fourfold higher infant titre or signs of disease carry more diagnostic weight than any single positive antibody result.
steps.say: A positive infant treponemal test may be maternal antibody; titre comparison and clinical signs decide risk.

nodes.label: Examine infant and compare RPR titre
Blood, CSF and long bone evaluation
Treat or closely follow by risk category

steps.tx: In neurosyphilis, **CSF VDRL** is specific but insensitive, so a reactive result strongly supports the diagnosis while a negative result does not exclude it. CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis and raised protein provide supportive evidence. Ocular syphilis and otosyphilis are clinical syndromes that can arise at any stage and are managed with a neurosyphilis regimen. Benzathine penicillin does not reliably reach treponemicidal CSF concentrations.
steps.say: Reactive CSF VDRL helps confirm neurosyphilis, but benzathine penicillin is not adequate central nervous system therapy.

left.title: CSF clues
points: Reactive VDRL is highly supportive
White cell count often lymphocyte predominant
Protein often elevated
Treponemal CSF tests are sensitive but nonspecific

right.title: Treatment point
points: Aqueous crystalline penicillin G intravenously
Benzathine penicillin does not treat CNS disease
Eye and ear disease use neurosyphilis approach
Follow CSF cell count and serum titres
